goal: mc owns the names it reads and writes. A proposal's filename says which system it is for, so the page counts proposals by system and a new proposal without the tag is named the moment it is written.

The runner makes a step's workarea only on a project branch it owns. A branch held by someone else's worktree, or carrying someone else's commits, blocks the step as `branch-foreign` and names the holder. A landed leftover branch is replaced by a fresh one from origin/main.
mc writes and checks its own hook registration in `~/.claude/settings.json` (`mc hook install [--check]`), and the page says when that registration has drifted.
A `per_repo` lane count changed with `mc run lanes` takes effect in a running runner without `mc run --update`.
contract: A proposal stays prose. mc reads only its filename and never parses what is inside it (`listProposals`, `src/mc/brief-collect.js`). Nothing renames a proposal file.
No step changes how the merger measures or lands a pull request.
The register stays the one place a step's state lives (ruling 21). No step writes plan state into PLAN.json except `met` in the last step.

`mc hook install` changes only mc's own entries in `~/.claude/settings.json`: entries whose command starts with `mc hook session-start` or `mc hook pre-tool`. It never prints the file, never deletes another entry and never overwrites a file it cannot parse.
A lane leaves its loop only between passes, never inside a step.
Every existing `mc run`, `mc helper`, `mc hook` and page behaviour not named in a step stays as it is.
out_of_scope: Renaming the proposals already in `~/mc/proposals/`. They are read, lead to an action, a project or nothing, and are archived (Martin, 2026-10-18); only new proposals carry the tag.
Renaming a newly written untagged proposal automatically. Guessing the system from the text is the parse that `brief-collect.js` removed.
A before/after check on the interactive `mc helper` desk and on step or plan sessions. They write proposals through their role text, and the page's `untagged` count is where a miss shows.
`plan-branch.js` `freePlanBranch` itself: its rule for a plan directory under `~/mc/plan/` stays as #900 left it.
Removing a scratchpad worktree that holds a project branch. The runner names it and a person removes it.
A drift warning in `mc hook session-start`. A session-start hook that runs is proof the registration exists, and the page is where Martin looks.
PostToolUse or any other hook event in `mc hook install`. It writes the two entries mc answers today.
Codex hook registration. Codex reads no Claude Code settings.
An ordering rule between lanes, and a lane already waiting for a total slot when its index goes above `per_repo`: that pass still runs its step.
Editing the frozen parts of `mc-runner-hardening`, including its out_of_scope sentence about `per_repo`.

success_criteria.criterion: Every role and prompt that names a proposal file names it `<date>-<system>-<slug>.md` with system `mc` or `memoro`. A new proposal from an intake turn whose name has no system gets `proposal <file> names no system (mc|memoro)` on the turn's line. The page's BRIEF line splits the count, for example `2 proposals · mc 1 · untagged 1`.
success_criteria.check: `node --test --import ./tests/_isolate-home.mjs tests/mc/helper-turn.test.js tests/mc/commands/helper.test.js tests/mc/page.test.js tests/mc/roles-decisions.test.js` passes, including the tests named in step 1.

success_criteria.criterion: When the runner makes a workarea, it blocks the step as `branch-foreign` if the project's local branch is checked out in a worktree outside the plan home or carries commits not on origin/main. The block names the holder. If the local branch has landed, no worktree holds it and no register step names it, the runner deletes it and creates the workarea from origin/main, and says so in one line.
success_criteria.check: `node --test --import ./tests/_isolate-home.mjs tests/mc/plan-branch.test.js tests/mc/run.test.js tests/mc/run-plan.test.js` passes, including the tests named in step 2.

success_criteria.criterion: `mc hook install` writes the SessionStart entry and the PreToolUse entry on `Bash|Write|Read` into `~/.claude/settings.json`. It leaves every other entry untouched, writes nothing on a second run and refuses a file that is not JSON. `--check` exits 1 on drift and 0 otherwise. The page's MC line names the drift and `mc hook install`.
success_criteria.check: `node --test --import ./tests/_isolate-home.mjs tests/mc/hooks.test.js tests/mc/commands/hook-install.test.js tests/mc/page.test.js` passes, including the tests named in step 3. `mc hook install --check` exits 0 on this machine after `mc hook install`.

success_criteria.criterion: A running runner starts a new lane within one poll when `per_repo` is raised. When `per_repo` is lowered, a lane whose number is now above it ends after the step it is in and starts nothing more. `mc run lanes` says both numbers apply now.
success_criteria.check: `node --test --import ./tests/_isolate-home.mjs tests/mc/run.test.js tests/mc/commands/run-lanes.test.js` passes, including the tests named in step 4.

steps.title: A proposal's filename names its system, and mc counts and checks by it
steps.done_when: The role files, `helperPrompt`, `helperLaunch` and the help text name proposals `<date>-<system>-<slug>.md`; `proposalSystem` in `src/mc/brief-collect.js` reads the tag; `describeTurn` names an untagged new proposal; the page's BRIEF line splits the count by system; the new and changed tests in `tests/mc/helper-turn.test.js`, `tests/mc/commands/helper.test.js`, `tests/mc/page.test.js` and `tests/mc/roles-decisions.test.js` pass; `mc gate` is green.
instruction: Why: on 2026-10-18 `~/mc/proposals/` held 104 files. Nothing outside their text said which system each was about. 100 carry a `System:` line in about fifty spellings (`memoro`, `` `memoro` (the deployed service) ``, `memoro-cli (mc), with a few lines in memoro …`), 4 carry none, and sorting them took a whole agent. The tag now goes in the filename, which mc already reads: `~/mc/proposals/<date>-<system>-<slug>.md`, system `mc` (memoro-cli) or `memoro` (the deployed service). `ls ~/mc/proposals/*-mc-*` is then the filter, and `mc` and `memoro` share no prefix that matters. Do not parse the file: `brief-collect.js` (comment above `listProposals`, lines 38-51) records why a frontmatter parse was removed. The proposal is `~/mc/proposals/2026-10-18-mc-proposals-name-their-system.md`. Renaming the existing files is not this step.

The reader, in `src/mc/brief-collect.js`. Add `basename` to the `node:path` import. Directly after `listProposals` (line 53) add: `/** The systems a proposal's filename may name: `<date>-<system>-<slug>.md`. One word per repository in `defaultRepos`; the list grows only when one joins. */ export const PROPOSAL_SYSTEMS = Object.freeze(['mc', 'memoro']);`. Then add `/** The system a proposal's filename names, `'mc'` or `'memoro'`, or null when the name carries none. Read off the name, never out of the file. */ export function proposalSystem(file) { const match = /^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}-(mc|memoro)-[^/]+\.md$/u.exec(basename(String(file || ''))); return match ? match[1] : null; }`.

The rule, in the role files. In `canon/roles/_common.md` lines 27-30, the paragraph becomes exactly: `What you found that is not your job is a proposal: one file per finding, `~/mc/proposals/<date>-<system>-<slug>.md`, where `<system>` is `mc` (memoro-cli, mc itself) or `memoro` (the deployed service): the one whose change would resolve it, the first when both would change. Inside it: prose, which system and why, what you read. Say so in one line and carry on.` The sentences after it, from `Not `~/mc/intake/``, stay unchanged. In `canon/roles/helper.md` lines 9-11, `one file per thing, `~/mc/proposals/<date>-<slug>.md`. The date and the `.md` are mc's: it counts what is there and orders by name.` becomes `one file per thing, `~/mc/proposals/<date>-<system>-<slug>.md`, system `mc` or `memoro`. The date, the system and the `.md` are mc's: it counts what is there by system and orders by name.` In `canon/roles/intake.md` line 13, ``~/mc/proposals/<date>-<slug>.md`` becomes ``~/mc/proposals/<date>-<system>-<slug>.md``, and the next sentence becomes `The date, the system and the `.md` are mc's; the prose is yours.` In intake.md's paragraph at line 23 (`You are also the only reader who has to say which system`), the sentence `Say it in the proposal, in its own words:` becomes `Say it in the filename (`mc` or `memoro`) and in the proposal, in its own words:`.

The prompts. In `src/mc/helper-turn.js`: line 10 becomes ` * one `~/mc/proposals/<date>-<system>-<slug>.md`, or none.` In `helperPrompt` (line 89), add `const tagOf = (repo) => (repo === 'memoro-cli' ? 'mc' : 'memoro');` at the top of the function body. Replace the comment at lines 92-95 with `// The filename's system is what the page counts by and what a person filters on. A turn left to infer it from a digest would get it right most days, and the days it did not would file a proposal against the wrong system, so a file whose name says which repository it is keeps saying so.` Line 108 becomes `out.push(`It is **${known}**'s, so a proposal you write about it is named \`${date}-${tagOf(known)}-<slug>.md\`.`);`. In the `else` branch (lines 113-114), the pushed text becomes `'Nothing in that name says which system the file belongs to, so decide it from what you read and put it in the name:', '`mc` for memoro-cli (mc itself on this machine), `memoro` for the deployed service.'`. Line 118 becomes `` `One file, one outcome: either **one** proposal in `${proposalsPath}`, named `${date}-<mc|memoro>-<slug>.md`,` ``. In `src/mc/commands/helper.js` `helperLaunch` (line 211), the line becomes `` ``${proposalsPath}` as `${date}-<mc|memoro>-<slug>.md` in the shape your role gives.` ``. In `src/mc/help-text.js` line 442, `~/mc/proposals/<date>-<x>.md. It` becomes `~/mc/proposals/<date>-<mc|memoro>-<x>.md.`, and `It` moves to the start of the next line. Rewrap that entry so that no line is longer than the longest line beside it.

The check: name a new untagged proposal, never rename it. In `src/mc/helper-turn.js`, add `proposalSystem` to the existing import from `./brief-collect.js` (line 40). `describeTurn` (line 143) becomes: `export function describeTurn({ wrote = [], waiting = [] }) { if (!wrote.length) return `no proposal — nothing in the file warranted one (${waiting.length} still waiting)`; const line = `${wrote.length} proposal${wrote.length === 1 ? '' : 's'}, ${waiting.length} waiting`; const untagged = wrote.filter((p) => typeof p?.file === 'string' && !proposalSystem(p.file)).map((p) => `proposal ${p.file} names no system (mc|memoro)`); return untagged.length ? `${line} — ${untagged.join('; ')}` : line; }`. Its two callers, `src/mc/run.js` line 2077 (the runner's intake drain) and `src/mc/commands/helper.js` line 129 (`mc helper --intake`), print that one line, so neither changes. Above the function add one comment line: the names come from the before/after listing in `runHelperTurn`, and a name without a system is said and left alone, because guessing it is the parse that was removed.

The page. In `src/mc/page-collect.js`, add `proposalSystem` to the import from `./brief-collect.js`; if the file has no such import, add one. In `intakeSection` (line 910), the returned object (line 937) becomes `{ repos, digests: repos.length, proposals: proposals.length, by_system: proposalCounts(proposals), proposal_files: proposalSummary(proposals) }`. Add next to `proposalSummary`: `/** The proposals by the system their filename names; a name with none is `untagged`, which is where the naming rule was not followed. */ function proposalCounts(files) { const counts = { mc: 0, memoro: 0, untagged: 0 }; for (const file of files) counts[proposalSystem(file) || 'untagged'] += 1; return counts; }`. In `src/mc/page-render.js` `briefLines` (line 649), in the `trailing([...])` call at lines 658-662, insert this right after the `${count} proposal…` part: `...[['mc', intake?.by_system?.mc], ['memoro', intake?.by_system?.memoro], ['untagged', intake?.by_system?.untagged]].filter(([, n]) => n > 0).map(([label, n]) => ({ text: `${label} ${n}`, styles: [label === 'untagged' ? 'yellow' : 'grey'] })),`. Add one sentence to the doc comment above `briefLines`: the count is split by the system in each filename, and `untagged` is drawn yellow.

Tests in `tests/mc/helper-turn.test.js`, `describe('what the turn is told')`. Line 180: the regex becomes `/2026-08-29-<mc\|memoro>-<slug>\.md/u`. In 'says which repository a digest is, and leaves any other file to the turn' (line 203): line 204 becomes `assert.match(helperPrompt({ file: FILE, now: NOW }), /It is \*\*memoro\*\*'s, so a proposal you write about it is named `2026-08-29-memoro-<slug>\.md`/u);`. Line 205's regex becomes `` /`2026-08-29-mc-<slug>\.md`/u ``. Line 209 becomes `assert.ok(!dropped.includes('is named `2026-08-29-'), 'no system is asserted for it');`. Line 210's regex becomes `/Nothing in that name says which system[\s\S]*put it in the name/u`. Line 212's regex becomes `` /`2026-08-29-mc-<slug>\.md`/u ``. Then add `describe('the system a proposal\'s name carries')` with one `it('is read from the name alone', …)`. Import `proposalSystem` from `../../src/mc/brief-collect.js`. Assert `proposalSystem('2026-10-18-mc-merger-gate.md')` is `'mc'`, `proposalSystem('/x/proposals/2026-10-18-memoro-sms-send.md')` is `'memoro'`, and `proposalSystem('2026-10-18-mcp-thing.md')`, `proposalSystem('2026-10-18-merger-gate.md')`, `proposalSystem('notes.md')` and `proposalSystem(null)` are all `null`.

Tests in `tests/mc/commands/helper.test.js`. Line 145 becomes ``assert.match(launch.prompt, /`\/work\/proposals` as `2026-08-30-<mc\|memoro>-<slug>\.md`/u);``. Line 177 becomes `assert.match(overlay, /<date>-<system>-<slug>\.md/u);`. In 'says what the turn produced in one line' (line 307), keep both existing asserts and add `assert.equal(describeTurn({ wrote: [{ file: '2026-08-29-mc-a.md' }], waiting: [1] }), '1 proposal, 1 waiting');` and `assert.equal(describeTurn({ wrote: [{ file: '2026-08-29-a.md' }], waiting: [1] }), '1 proposal, 1 waiting — proposal 2026-08-29-a.md names no system (mc|memoro)');`. The regex at line 204 still matches as a prefix, so leave it. In `tests/mc/roles-decisions.test.js` line 145, the regex becomes `/~\/mc\/proposals\/<date>-<system>-<slug>\.md/u`.

Tests in `tests/mc/page.test.js`, 'names the digest, its age and the proposals waiting' (line 1212). `proposals` becomes `['2026-08-29-mc-one.md', '2026-08-29-two.md']`. Add `assert.deepEqual(intake.by_system, { mc: 1, memoro: 0, untagged: 1 });`. The `proposal_files` deepEqual becomes `{ oldest: '2026-08-29', newest: '2026-08-29', newest_names: ['two', 'mc-one'] }`. The BRIEF line regex becomes `/^ {7}2 proposals · mc 1 · untagged 1 · 08-29 · newest two · mc-one$/u`. If another test in the file deep-compares a whole `intake` object, add `by_system` to the expected value there and change nothing else.

Docs. In `docs/technical/mc-helper.md`, the passage from line 367 (`Its output is zero or more `~/mc/proposals/<date>-<slug>.md`:`) through the frontmatter example after it describes a format that is gone. Replace it with one paragraph: the output is zero or more `~/mc/proposals/<date>-<system>-<slug>.md`, system `mc` or `memoro`, prose inside; the turn is told the system when the digest's name says it; and `describeTurn` names a new file whose name carries no system, which is never renamed. In `docs/technical/mc-ui.md` line 105-107 (BRIEF), the count is described as split by the system in each filename (`mc 23 · memoro 81 · untagged 2`), with `untagged` drawn yellow, and the slug as `<date>-<system>-<slug>.md`. Add `changelog.d/proposal-names-system.md` with `section: Changed` and one entry: **A proposal's filename names its system.** Give the why (104 files, prose `System:` lines in fifty spellings, an agent to sort them), the form `<date>-<mc|memoro>-<slug>.md`, the `names no system` line on an intake turn, and the page's split count.
In a final commit that touches nothing else, change `docs/mc-command-matrix.md` line 76 (`mc helper`): `~/mc/proposals/<date>-<x>.md` becomes `~/mc/proposals/<date>-<mc|memoro>-<x>.md`.

steps.title: The runner refuses a project branch it does not own (`branch-foreign`)
steps.done_when: `claimProjectBranch` in `src/mc/plan-branch.js` is asked before `addWorktree` in `runStepClaimed` (`src/mc/run.js`); a project branch held outside the plan home, or ahead of origin/main and named by no register step, blocks the step as `branch-foreign` naming the holder; a landed, unheld, unregistered one is deleted and the workarea made from origin/main with one runner.log line; `canon/roles/plan.md` and `planLaunch` name the PR branch `plan/<project>`; the new tests in `tests/mc/plan-branch.test.js`, `tests/mc/run.test.js` and `tests/mc/run-plan.test.js` pass; `mc gate` is green.
instruction: Why: on 2026-10-14T19:53:42Z `mc run` blocked `morning-calls` step 1 as `workarea worktree-missing`, four minutes after its plan landed (#13703). The register's reason was `git worktree add failed (fatal: 'morning-calls' is already used by worktree at '…/scratchpad/wt3')`. The planning session in `~/mc/plan/assistant` had opened its PR from a branch named after the project and kept it checked out in a worktree in its scratchpad. #900 (`src/mc/plan-branch.js` `freePlanBranch`, called at `src/mc/run.js` line 2247) frees such a branch only when its holder is under `~/mc/plan/`. A scratchpad holder gets `why: 'not a plan directory'`, and the step fails on git's raw message. There is a second fault under it. `addWorktree` (`src/mc/work-area.js` lines 342-352) checks out a branch that already exists rather than creating it from `origin/main`. With no holder, step 1 would have started silently on the planning branch's old pre-squash head, with no `PLAN.json` and behind `main`. The proposal is `~/mc/proposals/2026-10-14-plan-branch-takes-project-name.md`. `canon/roles/plan.md` line 15 already says `Never check out a branch named after a project` (since #783, 2026-10-06), and the session did it anyway. So mc has to own the name.

The rule. The runner uses an existing local branch `<project>` for a new workarea only when it is the runner's: a register step for the project names it as its `branch`. Otherwise: (a) a branch checked out in any worktree that `freePlanBranch` did not free is foreign; (b) a branch no worktree holds that has landed (`branchLanded` says `'landed'`) is a leftover, and is deleted so the workarea is created from origin/main, said in one line; (c) a branch no worktree holds that is `'ahead'` or `'unknown'` is foreign, because it may be someone's work. A foreign branch blocks the step with its own word, `branch-foreign`, and names the holder, so the reason says what to do.

In `src/mc/plan-branch.js`, after `freePlanBranch`, add and export `claimProjectBranch({ repo, branch, plan = null, registered = false, git })`, with `git(cwd, args)` returning `{ ok, stdout }` as in `freePlanBranch`. Body: `const out = (cwd, args) => { const r = git(cwd, args); return r?.ok ? String(r.stdout ?? '').trimEnd() : null; };` then `if (!git(repo, ['rev-parse', '-q', '--verify', `refs/heads/${branch}`])?.ok) return { verdict: 'absent', holder: null, why: null };` then `if (plan?.holder && !plan.freed) return { verdict: 'foreign', holder: plan.holder, why: plan.why || 'checked out there' };` then `if (registered) return { verdict: 'own', holder: null, why: null };` then `const landed = branchLanded(repo, branch, { run: (args) => out(repo, args) });` then `if (landed === 'landed') { if (!git(repo, ['branch', '-D', branch])?.ok) return { verdict: 'foreign', holder: null, why: 'it has landed and could not be deleted' }; return { verdict: 'recreated', holder: null, why: null }; }` and finally `return { verdict: 'foreign', holder: null, why: landed === 'ahead' ? 'it has commits that are not on origin/main' : 'whether it has landed could not be told' };`. Above it, a doc comment of a few lines: the project's branch name is the runner's; the four verdicts; why a landed leftover is replaced rather than checked out (its head is the pre-squash commit, behind main, and the 2026-10-14 case would have started on it); and why an `ahead` or `unknown` one is never touched (it may be work). Add one sentence to the file's header comment pointing to it.

In `src/mc/run.js` `runStepClaimed`, inside `if (!deps.exists(worktree)) {` (lines 2240-2251), between the `if (plan.freed) say(…)` line and `const added = deps.addWorktree(…)`, insert: `const registered = (readEntry(root, name, { read: deps.read })?.steps || []).some((step) => step?.branch === name);` `const claim = claimProjectBranch({ repo: repo.path, branch: name, plan, registered, git: deps.git });` `if (claim.verdict === 'foreign') return block(REFUSAL['branch-foreign'], `branch ${name} is not the runner's: ${claim.holder ? `checked out at ${claim.holder}` : 'no worktree holds it'} (${claim.why}) — remove that worktree or delete the branch, then mc step ready`);` `if (claim.verdict === 'recreated') say(`${name}: local branch ${name} had landed and no worktree held it — deleted, the workarea starts from origin/main`);`. `readEntry` is already imported (line 122) and `root` is in scope (line 628). Change the import at line 139 to `import { claimProjectBranch, freePlanBranch } from './plan-branch.js';`. Add one comment line above the new block: a project's branch is the runner's name, and one it did not make is never checked out (2026-10-14, `morning-calls`).

The word, in `src/mc/run-plan.js`. In `RUN_REFUSALS` (line 186), directly after the `worktree` entry, add `{ reason: 'branch-foreign', read: false, why: 'whose the project branch is, is asked of git and the register while the round makes the worktree, and the reading makes no worktree' },`. In `WORKAREA_BLOCKS` (line 230), after `worktree: 'worktree-missing',` add `'branch-foreign': 'branch-foreign',`. `REFUSAL['branch-foreign']` then exists, and `WORKAREA_BLOCK_NAMES` carries the name a plan can hold.

The role text. In `canon/roles/plan.md` line 15, after `the runner cannot make that project's workarea while you hold it.`, add: `Your pull request's branch is `plan/<project>`, and a worktree you make for it is removed once it is pushed. A project-named branch the runner did not make blocks its first step as `branch-foreign`.` In `src/mc/commands/plan.js` `planLaunch` (line 342), after the line `'`mc run` does can reach it.',` add `'A plan\'s pull request goes from a branch named `plan/<project>`, never `<project>`: that name is the runner\'s.',`. If a test in `tests/mc/commands/plan.test.js` compares the whole prompt text, add the line there too.

Tests in `tests/mc/plan-branch.test.js`, with its real-git `planned()` fixture. Add a `describe('claimProjectBranch')` after `describe('freePlanBranch')`, import `claimProjectBranch`, and add these cases. (1) 'a branch nobody has is absent': `claimProjectBranch({ repo: p.repo, branch: 'other', git })` deep-equals `{ verdict: 'absent', holder: null, why: null }`. (2) 'a branch held outside the plan home is foreign': `const p = planned({ under: 'elsewhere/scratchpad' }); const plan = freePlanBranch({ repo: p.repo, branch: 'proj', planRoot: p.planRoot, git, gh: noGh });`; then `claimProjectBranch({ repo: p.repo, branch: 'proj', plan, git })` deep-equals `{ verdict: 'foreign', holder: p.holder, why: 'not a plan directory' }`. (3) 'a landed branch no worktree holds is deleted': `const p = planned(); raw(p.repo, ['worktree', 'remove', p.holder]);`; the verdict is `'recreated'`, `git(p.repo, ['rev-parse', '--verify', 'refs/heads/proj']).ok` is false, and `git(p.repo, ['worktree', 'add', '-q', '-b', 'proj', join(p.root, 'step'), 'origin/main']).ok` is true. (4) 'an unlanded branch no worktree holds is foreign and kept': `planned({ landed: false })`, worktree removed the same way; the result deep-equals `{ verdict: 'foreign', holder: null, why: 'it has commits that are not on origin/main' }` and `refs/heads/proj` still verifies. (5) 'a branch the register names is the runner's own': as (4) with `registered: true`; the verdict is `'own'` and the branch still verifies.

Tests in `tests/mc/run.test.js`. (a) In `BLOCKS` (line 3847), after the `worktree-missing` case, add `{ block: 'branch-foreign', reason: 'branch-foreign', what: 'a project branch checked out in a worktree the runner does not own', make: scratchHeld, detail: /branch m is not the runner's: checked out at /tmp/scratchpad/wt3 \(not a plan directory\) — remove that worktree or delete the branch/u }`. Above `BLOCKS`, define `const scratchHeld = () => { const f = fixture({ plans: { memoro: { m: ready } }, refs: { memoro: ['m'] }, session: okSession() }); const git = f.deps.git; f.deps.git = (cwd, args) => (args[0] === 'worktree' && args[1] === 'list' ? { ok: true, stdout: 'worktree /home/memoro
HEAD abc
branch refs/heads/main

worktree /tmp/scratchpad/wt3
HEAD eb261c5d6a
branch refs/heads/m
' } : git(cwd, args)); return f; };`. `refs: { memoro: ['m'] }` is what makes `rev-parse -q --verify refs/heads/m` in `/home/memoro` succeed in the fixture's git stub (line 306). (b) In `CASES` (line 4098), after the `worktree` case, add `{ reason: 'branch-foreign', what: 'the project branch is held by a worktree the runner does not own', make: scratchHeld }`. It is `read: false`, so the agreement test expects the reading to say runnable. (c) A new test after the `BLOCKS` loop: 'a landed project branch no worktree holds is deleted and the step starts from origin/main': `fixture({ plans: { memoro: { m: ready } }, refs: { memoro: ['m'] }, landed: ['m'], session: okSession() })`, `const runner = createRunner({ deps: f.deps }); await runner.runStep('m', runner.queue());`. Assert `f.calls.git.some((c) => c[0] === '/home/memoro' && c[1] === 'branch' && c[2] === '-D' && c[3] === 'm')`, assert the runner.log matches `/m: local branch m had landed and no worktree held it — deleted, the workarea starts from origin/main/u`, and assert `f.calls.sessions.length` is 1. (d) 'an unlanded project branch no worktree holds blocks as branch-foreign': the same fixture without `landed`; the outcome is `'skipped:branch-foreign'`, `f.calls.sessions.length` is 0, the log matches `/branch m is not the runner's: no worktree holds it \(it has commits that are not on origin/main\)/u`, and no `branch -D` call was made. In `tests/mc/run-plan.test.js` line 1051, the expected keys become `['branch', 'branch-foreign', 'dirty', 'role-missing', 'sync', 'tool-missing', 'worktree']`.

Docs. In `docs/technical/mc-run.md`, the table at lines 448-455 gains the row `| `branch-foreign` | `branch-foreign` | 2 — the project's local branch is held by a worktree the runner did not free, or has commits not on origin/main and no register step names it; the holder is named |`. Under the table, add one paragraph: a landed local branch that no worktree holds and no register step names is deleted and recreated from origin/main, said in runner.log (`morning-calls`, 2026-10-14). In `docs/project/README.md` line 67, add `branch-foreign` to the list of workarea names after `worktree-missing`. In `docs/technical/mc-plan.md`, after the paragraph ending at line 184, add: since 2026-10-14 the role and the launch prompt also name the PR branch `plan/<project>`, and the runner refuses a project-named branch it did not make as `branch-foreign` instead of failing inside `git worktree add`. Add `changelog.d/branch-foreign.md` with `section: Fixed`: **The runner uses a project branch only when it is its own.** Give the morning-calls case, the two faults, the `branch-foreign` word, and the landed-leftover rule.

steps.title: `mc hook install [--check]` writes and checks mc's hook registration, and the page names drift
steps.done_when: `MC_HOOKS`, `hookRegistration`, `installHooks`, `hookDrift` and `readClaudeSettings` exist in `src/mc/hooks.js`; `mc hook install` writes mc's two entries into `~/.claude/settings.json` idempotently and `--check` exits 1 on drift; `mcSection` carries `hooks` and the page's MC line names it; the new tests in `tests/mc/hooks.test.js`, `tests/mc/commands/hook-install.test.js` and `tests/mc/page.test.js` pass; the help text and the matrix row are in their own final commit; `mc gate` is green.
instruction: Why: mc's hook registration is pasted by hand from `usage()` in `src/mc/commands/hook.js` and drifts without anyone seeing. `mc-runner-hardening` step 8 makes `mc hook pre-tool` run the repositories' own PreToolUse hooks, memoro's `block-sqlite-state.sh` among them on `Read`, and changes the documented matcher to `Bash|Write|Read`. But the live `~/.claude/settings.json` stays at `Bash|Write` until someone edits it, so the Read half never fires. Nothing in `src/mc` reads or writes that file today. mc should write and check its own lines. This step starts after `mc-runner-hardening` step 8 has merged: read `src/mc/hooks.js` and `src/mc/commands/hook.js` as they are then, because that step changes both. The file holds other entries, for example a `block-secret-reads.sh` PreToolUse entry on `Bash|Read`, and possibly secrets elsewhere. Never print its contents, in output, in an error message or in a test failure.

In `src/mc/hooks.js`, add `readFileSync` to the `node:fs` import if step 8 has not already, and add `homedir` from `node:os`. Add, after `inMcTerritory`: (1) `export const MC_HOOKS = Object.freeze([Object.freeze({ event: 'SessionStart', which: 'session-start', matcher: null, command: 'mc hook session-start 2>/dev/null || true' }), Object.freeze({ event: 'PreToolUse', which: 'pre-tool', matcher: 'Bash|Write|Read', command: 'mc hook pre-tool 2>/dev/null || true' })]);` with a comment: what `mc hook install` writes; `|| true` because a hook must never stand between a session and its work; `Read` so the repositories' Read hooks answer through pre-tool. (2) `export function claudeSettingsPath(home = homedir()) { return join(home, '.claude', 'settings.json'); }`. (3) `export function readClaudeSettings(path, { readFileSync: read = readFileSync } = {})`, which returns the parsed object, or `null` when the file is missing, unreadable, not JSON, or not a plain object. It never throws.

(4) `export function hookRegistration(settings)`, which returns `{ ok, problems }`. For each `want` of `MC_HOOKS`: take `const entries = Array.isArray(settings?.hooks?.[want.event]) ? settings.hooks[want.event] : [];` and keep those whose `hooks` array has a hook with `type === 'command'` and a `command` matching `new RegExp(`^mc hook ${want.which}\\b`, 'u')`. None: push `{ which: want.which, have: null, want }`. More than one: push `{ which: want.which, have: 'twice', want }`. One: let `matcher = entry.matcher || null` and `command` be that hook's command; if `matcher !== want.matcher` or `command !== want.command`, push `{ which: want.which, have: { matcher, command }, want }`. `ok` is `problems.length === 0`. (5) `export function hookDrift({ problems })`, which returns `null` for no problems, else one short phrase per problem joined by `, `: `${which} not registered`, `${which} registered twice`, `${which} on ${have.matcher || 'every tool'}, want ${want.matcher}` when the matcher differs, otherwise `${which} runs another command`. (6) `export function installHooks(settings)`, which returns a new object and never changes its argument (`structuredClone`). Ensure `next.hooks` is a plain object and `next.hooks[event]` an array. For each `want`: find the first entry holding an mc command for `want.which`. If there is one, set its `matcher` to `want.matcher` (delete the key when `want.matcher` is null), replace that hook with `{ type: 'command', command: want.command }`, and remove every other hook for the same `which` from other entries of that event, dropping an entry whose `hooks` becomes empty. If there is none, push `{ ...(want.matcher ? { matcher: want.matcher } : {}), hooks: [{ type: 'command', command: want.command }] }`. Every other key and entry keeps its value and order.

In `src/mc/commands/hook.js`, before the existing argument check, add `if (which === 'install') return install(extra, { stdout, stderr, deps });`, and write `install`. Arguments: anything but `--check` prints `mc: mc hook install takes only --check` plus `usage()` to stderr and returns 2. Path: `(deps.claudeSettingsPath || claudeSettingsPath)(deps.home)`. Read: `deps.readFile ? deps.readFile(path) : readFileSync(path, 'utf8')`. ENOENT means start from `{}`. Any other read error, a parse error or a parsed value that is not a plain object means: write `mc: ${path} could not be read as JSON — nothing written` and return 1. Never include the error's message, because a JSON parse error quotes the file. Then `const before = hookRegistration(settings)`. With `--check`: when `before.ok`, print `mc: hooks registered in ${path}` and return 0; otherwise print `mc: ${hookDrift(before)} — mc hook install writes them` and return 1. Without it: when `before.ok`, print `mc: hooks already registered in ${path}` and return 0; otherwise `(deps.writeJson || writeJsonAtomic)(path, installHooks(settings))` (`src/mc/atomic-write.js`), print `mc: hooks registered in ${path} (${hookDrift(before)} before)` and return 0. `usage()` builds its two `In ~/.claude/settings.json:` example lines from `MC_HOOKS`, and adds one line: `mc hook install [--check]  writes those two entries, or says whether they are there (exit 1 when not)`. Update the file's header comment for the third subcommand.

The page. In `src/mc/page-collect.js`, import `claudeSettingsPath, hookDrift, hookRegistration, readClaudeSettings` from `./hooks.js`. `collectPage` (line 1420) gets a new parameter, `claudeSettings = () => (env.HOME ? readClaudeSettings(claudeSettingsPath(env.HOME)) : null)`, with a comment: injected so that no test reads the real file; an env without HOME means none is read. In the `mcSection({ … })` call (line 1618), add `hooks: (() => { const settings = claudeSettings(); return settings ? hookDrift(hookRegistration(settings)) : null; })(),`. `mcSection` (line 979) takes `hooks = null`, and the returned object gains `...(hooks ? { hooks } : {}),` after `behind`, so a page with no drift keeps its exact old shape. In `src/mc/page-render.js` `mcLine` (line 1406), insert a part after `state` in the heading call at line 1440: `trailing([...lead, fits ? state : { ...state, text: short }, { text: info.hooks ? `hooks: ${info.hooks} · mc hook install` : '', styles: ['yellow'] }, ...rest])`. Then grep `collectPage(` in `tests/` and add `claudeSettings: () => null` to every call whose env does not set HOME, so that no test depends on this machine's file.

Tests in `tests/mc/hooks.test.js`, a new `describe('mc hook install — mc\'s own registration')` before `describe('mc hook — the door')`, importing the new names. Fixture: `const FOREIGN = { matcher: 'Bash|Read', hooks: [{ type: 'command', command: '/x/block-secret-reads.sh' }] };` and `const OLD = { permissions: { allow: ['Bash'] }, hooks: { PreToolUse: [FOREIGN, { matcher: 'Bash|Write', hooks: [{ type: 'command', command: 'mc hook pre-tool 2>/dev/null || true' }] }], SessionStart: [{ hooks: [{ type: 'command', command: 'mc hook session-start 2>/dev/null || true' }] }] } };`. Cases: (1) `hookRegistration(OLD).problems` has one problem, `which: 'pre-tool'`, and `hookDrift(hookRegistration(OLD))` is `'pre-tool on Bash|Write, want Bash|Write|Read'`. (2) `hookDrift(hookRegistration({}))` is `'session-start not registered, pre-tool not registered'`. (3) `const next = installHooks(OLD)`: `hookRegistration(next).ok` is true; `next.hooks.PreToolUse[0]` deep-equals `FOREIGN`; `next.permissions` deep-equals `{ allow: ['Bash'] }`; `OLD.hooks.PreToolUse[1].matcher` is still `'Bash|Write'` (the argument was not changed); and `installHooks(next)` deep-equals `next`. (4) Two mc pre-tool entries reduce to one: `installHooks({ hooks: { PreToolUse: [{ matcher: 'Bash', hooks: [{ type: 'command', command: 'mc hook pre-tool' }] }, { matcher: 'Write', hooks: [{ type: 'command', command: 'mc hook pre-tool 2>/dev/null || true' }] }] } })` has exactly one PreToolUse entry, and that entry deep-equals `{ matcher: 'Bash|Write|Read', hooks: [{ type: 'command', command: 'mc hook pre-tool 2>/dev/null || true' }] }`. (5) `readClaudeSettings('/nope/settings.json')` is null, and with `readFileSync: () => '{oops'` it is null.

Tests in a new `tests/mc/commands/hook-install.test.js`, through `run` from `src/mc/commands/hook.js`, with a temp home (`mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), 'mc-hook-install-'))`, `mkdirSync(join(home, '.claude'))`) passed as `deps.home`, and `sink()` as in hooks.test.js. Cases: (1) 'installs into a file with old lines and keeps the rest': write `OLD` (copy it from hooks.test.js) to `.claude/settings.json`; `run(['install', '--check'], …)` returns 1 and its stdout matches `/pre-tool on Bash\|Write, want Bash\|Write\|Read — mc hook install writes them/u`; `run(['install'], …)` returns 0 and its stdout matches `/hooks registered in .*settings\.json \(pre-tool on Bash\|Write, want Bash\|Write\|Read before\)/u`; the file read back has `permissions` unchanged, the foreign entry first, and `hookRegistration(...).ok` true; `run(['install'])` again prints `/already registered/u`, and the file's mtime and text are unchanged; `run(['install', '--check'])` returns 0. (2) 'a missing file is created': no settings file; `run(['install'])` returns 0 and the file exists with both entries. (3) 'a file that is not JSON is refused and left alone': write `{"apiKey": "sk-secret", oops`; `run(['install'])` returns 1, stderr matches `/could not be read as JSON — nothing written/u` and does not contain `sk-secret`, and the file text is unchanged. (4) 'anything but --check is refused': `run(['install', '--force'])` returns 2.

Tests in `tests/mc/page.test.js`, `describe('MC')` (line 2210), using its `draw` and `UP`: 'names hook drift and the verb that mends it': `assert.match(draw(mcSection({ process: UP, commit: 'abc1234', behind: 0, hooks: 'pre-tool on Bash|Write, want Bash|Write|Read', now: NOW }), 200), /^ {2}MC {2}0\.7\.11 · up to date · hooks: pre-tool on Bash\|Write, want Bash\|Write\|Read · mc hook install · runner up 120 min · on abc1234$/u);`. Also `assert.equal('hooks' in mcSection({ process: UP, now: NOW }), false)`. In the `collectPage` test at line 2214, pass `claudeSettings: () => ({ hooks: {} })` and assert `data.mc.hooks` is `'session-start not registered, pre-tool not registered'`; drop the `hooks` key before the existing `deepEqual`, which otherwise stays as it is.

Docs. In `docs/technical/mc-hooks.md` § *Where they are registered* (line 20), say that `mc hook install` writes the block shown, changing only entries whose command starts with `mc hook session-start` or `mc hook pre-tool`; that `--check` exits 1 on drift; and that the page's MC line names drift as `hooks: … · mc hook install`. The JSON example's matcher becomes `Bash|Write|Read` (step 8 may already have done this). Add `changelog.d/hook-install.md` with `section: Added`: **`mc hook install [--check]`: mc writes and checks its own hook registration.** Give the why (pasted by hand, drifted, the Read matcher step 8 needs) and the page line. Then, in a final commit that touches nothing else: in `src/mc/help-text.js`, after the `mc hook pre-tool` entry (around line 294), add `  mc hook install [--check]        Write mc's two hook entries into ~/.claude/settings.json, changing no other entry; --check only says whether they are there (exit 1 when not)`, wrapped as its neighbours are, and add ` | install` to the summary line at line 43 if it still fits the column. In `docs/mc-command-matrix.md`, after the `mc log` row (line 77), add the row `| `mc hook install [--check]` | mc's own hook registration in `~/.claude/settings.json`: the SessionStart entry and the PreToolUse entry on `Bash\|Write\|Read`, written in place of older mc entries and beside everything else, idempotent, never over a file that is not JSON. `--check` writes nothing and exits 1 on drift. The page's MC line names drift. |`.

`mc gate tests/mc/hooks.test.js tests/mc/commands/hook-install.test.js tests/mc/page.test.js`, then `mc gate`, `mc publish`, `mc merge memoro-cli <pr>`. After the merge, with `mc` on PATH at the merged code, run `mc hook install` and then `mc hook install --check`, which must exit 0. Do not print the settings file.
comments: Blocked on `mc-runner-hardening` step 8 (`mc hook pre-tool applies the repositories' own PreToolUse hooks when the session started outside them`). That step changes `src/mc/hooks.js`, `src/mc/commands/hook.js` `usage()` and the documented matcher to `Bash|Write|Read`. Set this step `ready` with `mc step ready mc-ownership 3` once that step has merged.

steps.title: A `per_repo` changed with `mc run lanes` takes effect in a running runner
steps.done_when: `runLoop` in `src/mc/run.js` keeps a live set of lane loops: a raised `per_repo` starts the new lanes within one poll, and a lane whose index is at or above a lowered `per_repo` exits between passes; `mc run lanes` and `lane-count.js` say both numbers apply now; the new tests in `tests/mc/run.test.js` and the changed ones in `tests/mc/commands/run-lanes.test.js` pass; `mc gate` is green.
instruction: Why: `mc-runner-hardening` step 7 makes the total cap live (`takeSlot` reads `lanes.json` on each call through `capNow()`) and leaves `per_repo` structural. `runLoop` reads `laneSetting` once (`src/mc/run.js` line 3262 on 2026-10-18), `const { per_repo: count, total } = laneSetting;` fixes `count` (line 3401), and the lanes are a fixed `runner.repos.flatMap((repo) => Array.from({ length: count }, (_, index) => lane(repo, index)))` awaited with `Promise.all([...lanes, choreLoop()])` (lines 3519-3520). So `mc run lanes 3` on a running runner does nothing until `mc run --update`, which costs a handover. This step starts after `mc-runner-hardening` step 7 has merged: read `runLoop`, `createRunner`'s slot code, `lanes` in `src/mc/commands/run.js` and the header of `src/mc/lane-count.js` as they are then. Line numbers below are from 2026-10-18 and will have moved.

Design: a live lane set, reconciled on every poll slice. In `runLoop`'s unattended branch: (1) `const perRepoNow = () => (deps.laneCount || readLaneCount)().per_repo;` `readLaneCount` already clamps it to 1-8 with default 1. (2) `const live = new Map();`, keyed `${repo.name}#${index}`, each value a promise `lane(repo, index).then((result) => ({ key, result }))`. (3) `function reconcile()`: return at once if `runner.stopRequested() || runner.updateRequested() || handedOver`. Otherwise, with `const n = perRepoNow()`, for each repo and each `index < n` whose key is not in `live`, start it, and, when the start is not the initial one, say `lanes: ${n} per repository now — ${repo.name}#${index + 1} started`. Mark the initial call with a `let starting = true` that is cleared after it. (4) Replace the fixed `lanes` array and the `Promise.all` with: `const chores = choreLoop(); reconcile(); starting = false; const results = []; while (live.size) { const { key, result } = await Promise.race(live.values()); live.delete(key); results.push(result); } results.push(await chores);`. The two exit lines after it stay as they are, reading `results`.

The poll. `nap` (around line 3434) becomes `const nap = async (ms, { until = () => false } = {}) => { for (let left = ms; left > 0; left -= UPDATE_POLL_MS) { if (runner.stopRequested() || runner.updateRequested() || until()) return; reconcile(); await deps.sleep(Math.min(left, UPDATE_POLL_MS)); } };`. Every idle lane and the idle chore loop then reconcile once per `UPDATE_POLL_MS` slice, with no extra loop and no extra `deps.sleep` call. Also call `reconcile()` once after each `await runner.chores()` in `choreLoop`.

The lane. In `lane(repo, index)` (around line 3459): `const retired = () => index >= perRepoNow();`. The `tag` is no longer a constant. Compute it at the top of each loop pass as `const tag = index > 0 || perRepoNow() > 1 ? `${repo.name}#${index + 1}` : repo.name;`, and move it inside the `for (;;)`. Do not use `count` anywhere in the lane any more. At the top of the `for (;;)`, after the `updateRequested` check, add `if (retired()) { runner.say(`${tag}: per_repo is now ${perRepoNow()} — this lane exits`); return { retired: true }; }`. The idle nap becomes `await nap(idleSleepMs, { until: retired });`. The check sits only at the top of a pass, so a lane in a step finishes it, and a pass that has already begun waiting for a total slot still runs its step. Index 0 never retires, because `per_repo` is at least 1. A retired lane's key leaves `live`, so a later raise starts it again. Leave the `laneHolder` wait unchanged: a successor's lane waiting on its predecessor's file is not a running step, so let it retire through the same top-of-loop check as well.

The start line, around line 3401: `const { per_repo: count, total } = laneSetting;` stays only for the existing `lanes: N per repository, …` line, which is unchanged. Rewrite the comment above `runLoop`'s `laneSetting` read (around lines 3257-3261, as step 7 left it): both numbers are read live; `per_repo` by `reconcile` on every poll slice, which starts the missing lanes, and by each lane at the top of a pass, which ends a lane above it; `total` by `takeSlot`. Rewrite the doc comment at line 2094 (`per_repo needs nothing like this because it is structural`, as step 7 left it): `per_repo` is still structural, since there are that many lane loops per repository at any moment, but the set of loops follows `lanes.json`.

The verb and the setting. In `src/mc/commands/run.js` `lanes` (around lines 145-152), the written case's first line becomes `` `lanes ${phrase(pair, repos)} — applies now` `` and its last line becomes `'a running runner takes both at once: a new lane starts within half a minute, a lane above the new count ends after the step it is in'`, replacing whatever step 7 left there. In `src/mc/lane-count.js`, the header sentence about when the runner reads the numbers (as step 7 left it) becomes: `The runner reads both live: `total` each time a step is about to start, `per_repo` on every poll, starting a missing lane or ending one above it after its step. Neither needs `mc run --update`.` In `docs/technical/mc-run.md` around line 1001, `read once at start; a running runner takes a new count on `mc run --update`` becomes `read live: a raised count starts the new lanes within one poll (`UPDATE_POLL_MS`), a lowered one ends each lane above it after the step it is in`. In the paragraph around line 1054, add after `per_repo is structural …`: `— the number of loops follows lanes.json, so it binds within one poll of a change.`.

Tests in `tests/mc/run.test.js`, after 'runLoop: two lanes on one repository take the next two runnable names, never the same one' (line 3556), following its pattern: `fixture`, a session wrapper that records `starts` and waits on a shared `held` promise, `f.deps.sleep = () => new Promise((resolve) => { setImmediate(resolve); })`, and `const turns = async (n = 40) => { for (let i = 0; i < n; i += 1) await new Promise((resolve) => { setImmediate(resolve); }); };`. (1) 'runLoop: a per_repo raised while the runner runs starts the new lane': plans `{ memoro: { a: ready, b: ready } }`, `let per = 1; f.deps.laneCount = () => ({ per_repo: per, total: null });`, `const run = runLoop({ deps: f.deps }); await turns();`. `starts` is `['a']`. Then `per = 2; await turns(80);`. `starts` is `['a', 'b']`, and the runner.log matches `/lanes: 2 per repository now — memoro#2 started/u` and `/memoro#2: next — b /u`. Then `f.files['/w/runner/STOP'] = ''; release(); assert.equal(await run, 0);`. (2) 'runLoop: a per_repo lowered while the runner runs ends the lane above it after its step': plans `{ memoro: { a: ready, b: ready, c: ready } }`, `let per = 2`, run and `await turns()`. `starts` deep-equals `['a', 'b']`. Then `per = 1; release(); await turns(120);`. The runner.log matches `/memoro#2: per_repo is now 1 — this lane exits/u` and does not match `/memoro#2: next — c /u`; `starts` contains `'c'` exactly once; `starts.filter((n) => n === 'b').length` is 1. Then STOP and `assert.equal(await run, 0)`. If an existing `runLoop` test fails because a lane's tag changed from `memoro` to `memoro#1` while `per_repo` was raised in that test, fix the expectation; change no other assertion.

Tests in `tests/mc/commands/run-lanes.test.js`, 'lanes: the positional sets per_repo and --total sets the total, neither touching the other' (around line 79). The four expected first lines end in ` — applies now` in place of the ending step 7 left, for example `'lanes 4 per repository, no total cap (up to 8 across 2 repositories) — applies now'`. The regex on `per.out.at(-1)` becomes `/a running runner takes both at once: a new lane starts within half a minute, a lane above the new count ends after the step it is in/u`. Add `changelog.d/per-repo-live.md` with `section: Changed`: **A new lane count takes effect without `mc run --update`.** Give the why (a handover for a number) and what a raise and a lower each do.

`mc gate tests/mc/run.test.js`, `mc gate tests/mc/commands/run-lanes.test.js`, then `mc gate`, `mc publish`, `mc merge memoro-cli <pr>`. This is the plan's last step: in the same PR set every `success_criteria[].met` in this plan to true.
comments: Blocked on `mc-runner-hardening` step 7 (`The total lane cap is read live and counts every live runner's steps`). That step changes `createRunner`'s slot code, the `runLoop` comment, the `mc run lanes` lines and the `lane-count.js` header that this step rewrites. Set this step `ready` with `mc step ready mc-ownership 4` once that step has merged. If step 3 is still blocked then, it is a different blocker, and this step does not depend on step 3's code.
